title: Taskiem connector manifest (connector/v1)
description: Declarative description of a connector. Cross-reference rules (reconcile and compensate actions exist, idempotency encodings fit provider limits, pii fields exist in the input schema) are enforced at registration and documented in docs/contracts/connector-v1.md.

kind.description: rail: moves money, and Taskiem builds products on it; product: runs a whole process itself, and Taskiem connects to it and works around it; tool: anything else. Default tool (decision 0044).

egress_hosts.description: Hosts this connector may reach through the egress proxy; defaults to the base_url host.

connection_hosts.description: The hosts a connection's fields may name (rule 19), where the provider keeps each account in one place (Zoho's data centres): exact hosts, or *.<domain> for its subdomains. A ${connection.<field>} egress host or OAuth URL naming any other is refused. Required for OAuth URLs that start with ${connection.<field>}.

capabilities.description: What this rail can do, in Taskiem's words (schemas/capabilities-v1.json): each entry maps one capability to this connector's own actions (rule 16). Rails only.

events.description: The normalised payment events this rail's triggers produce (payout.settled, payment.received...), each from one trigger (rule 16).

mapping.description: Field names to values: a string starting with = is an expression, anything else is taken as it is.

input.description: The action's input, from the capability's (roots: input).

steps.description: Several actions for one capability, in order (Paystack: create_recipient, then transfer). A step's input may read earlier steps' outputs (steps.<id>.output).

output.description: The capability's output, from the action's (roots: input, output: the last action's, steps).

requires.description: Optional capability inputs this rail cannot do without (iswallet pays from a named wallet: source).

unsupported.description: Optional capability inputs this rail cannot honour; a step that gives one is refused rather than ignored (Paystack refunds in full: amount_kobo).

ignores.description: Capability inputs this rail does not need; dropped when given (a checkout that asks no phone number: customer.phone).

fixed.description: Capability inputs this rail takes with one value only (currency: NGN); a step that gives another is refused.

unsafe.description: The action is an unsafe_write and the capability allows one: an unknown outcome parks for a person.

settles_by.description: How a pending payout is followed to its end: the trigger whose payout events report it, and the capability that looks it up.

transfer.description: collect_transfer only, and required there: what the rail does with a transfer after the account expires and with a wrong amount, and the lifetimes it allows, in minutes.

when.description: Which of the trigger's deliveries are this event (roots: body, headers, query, item).

help.description: One line, in plain words, for the person connecting.

where.description: Where the value is in the provider's dashboard, e.g. Paystack → Settings → API Keys & Webhooks.

link.description: The provider's page that shows the value.

prefixes.description: What a right value starts with; mode names a choice offered to the person (live or test), shown with its label.

refuse.description: Values that are the wrong one (a public key), refused with a plain message.

multiline.description: The value spans lines (a PEM key): the person pastes it into a text area.

generate.description: A value Taskiem makes for the person: rsa_key_pair makes an RSA key pair in their browser, keeps the private key as the value and shows the public key to paste into the provider's dashboard.

modes.description: Live and test as separate hosts (rule 17): the person chooses one when connecting, the connection keeps it, and its calls go to that mode's base_url. For providers whose keys say the mode, use prefixes instead.

base_url.description: The mode's host; left out when only the deployment knows it (a production address issued at go-live), so the mode is offered only once it is set.

client.description: The platform app connections in this mode are linked with by OAuth (rule 20), where it is not auth.oauth2.client: Intuit's development keys reach only sandbox companies.

oauth2.description: How a connection is made by OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant with PKCE (docs/connector-sdk.md). A URL may start with ${server}/ to be resolved from the connector's base_url at runtime.

authorize_params.description: Extra query parameters on the consent URL (Google: access_type offline, prompt consent, for a refresh token).

platform_client_fields.description: Auth fields filled from Taskiem's own registration with the provider, for connectors that refresh tokens themselves: id and secret.

client.description: The platform app Taskiem registered with the provider (rule 18; decision 0051): TASKIEM_OAUTH_<CLIENT>_* in the environment. Several connectors may share one (zoho for Books, Mail and CRM). Default: the connector's id.

account_field.description: The auth field holding the provider account a connection is for (Slack's team id, a QuickBooks realm id): events Taskiem's app receives for that account are delivered to the connections that hold it (triggers with delivery: app).

fields_from_callback.description: Auth fields filled from the query parameters the provider sends the browser back with (QuickBooks' realmId; Zoho's location and accounts-server).

fields_from_token.description: Auth fields filled from the token answer: a field of the answer, a field of an object in it (team.id), one element of a list field (project_ids[0]), or ${server}.

scope_separator.description: What joins the scopes on the consent URL: a space (default, RFC 6749) or a comma (Slack).

client_auth.description: How Taskiem's client proves itself at the token URL (rule 20): body (default; client_id and client_secret in the form) or basic (HTTP Basic, RFC 6749 section 2.3.1; Intuit's).

token_method.description: How the code is exchanged (rule 21): post (default, RFC 6749) or get (the parameters in the query; Meta's Graph API).

linked_fields.description: Auth fields the connector's Link handler fills when a connection is made by OAuth, before it is saved (rule 21: Meta's Page, its token and its Instagram account).

revoke_encoding.description: The revoke request's body (rule 20): form (default, RFC 7009) or json ({"token": ...}; Intuit's).

field.description: Input field (or header:<Name>) that carries the encoded key.

length.description: Characters of encoded hash, excluding the prefix.

limits.description: The provider's own constraints on the field; registration checks prefix + encoded hash against them.

charset.description: Allowed characters as a regex character-class body, e.g. a-z0-9_-

scheme.description: body_token: the JSON body's field (field) carries the shared secret itself, which the provider was given when the subscription was made (Zoho CRM's watch token; compared in constant time). svix: Svix's (Standard Webhooks) base64 HMAC-SHA256 of '<svix-id>.<svix-timestamp>.<raw body>' under the base64 key after the secret's whsec_, any of svix-signature's space-separated 'v1,<base64>' values matching; the timestamp within tolerance (default 5m). header_secret: the header carries the shared secret itself (compared in constant time). path_secret: the URL's path form /{env}/{connection}/{token} carries the shared secret (for providers whose callback URLs may not carry a query string). connector: the connector's own code verifies (for signatures no scheme describes). slack_v0: HMAC-SHA256 over 'v0:<timestamp>:<raw body>', the header carrying 'v0=<hex>'.

encoding.description: hmac_*: how the signature header encodes the MAC (default hex; base64_of_hex is base64 of the lowercase hex string).

key_derivation.description: hmac_*: the MAC key is the secret itself (none, default) or the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the secret.

field.description: body_token: the JSON body's top-level field carrying the shared secret.

query.description: query_secret: the URL parameter carrying the shared secret (for providers that sign nothing; the callback URL is registered with it).

timestamp_header.description: hmac_sha256_timestamped: header with the unix-seconds timestamp; the signed string is '<timestamp>.<raw body>'.

tolerance.description: hmac_sha256_timestamped: reject timestamps further than this from now (default 5m).

signature_format.description: hmac_sha256_timestamped: the header carries 't=<unix>,v1=<hex>[,v1=<hex>...]', timestamp and signatures together, instead of a separate timestamp_header; any v1 value may match (a provider signing with an old and a new secret while it rotates).

ack.description: The answer a provider expects to an accepted delivery, instead of 202 JSON.

handshake.description: How the provider proves the endpoint before (or while) delivering. GET: the provider sends token_query equal to the connection's secret_field (for delivery: app, the app's verify token) and expects respond back as text (Meta). POST: a verified delivery for which when holds is answered with respond, not delivered (Slack url_verification).

split.description: A list-valued expression: each element becomes one event, seen by event_type, dedup and correlation as item (for providers that batch several events in one delivery).

delivery.description: connection (default): deliveries come to each connection's own URL under a tenant's hooks. both: either, so a business may bring its own app (its connection's secret_field verifies) or connect through Taskiem's (Slack). app: the provider sends every business's events to the one URL of Taskiem's platform app, /hooks/apps/<connector>/<trigger>; they are verified with the app's secret (TASKIEM_OAUTH_<CLIENT>_WEBHOOK_SECRET) and delivered to the connections whose account_field holds account_key (rule 18).

example.description: An example delivery as a run sees it: its body and, for a split trigger, one item (dry runs and the docs).

pii.description: Personal data in a delivery (rule 21): paths under the run's trigger (body.entry.*.messaging.*.message.text, item.message.text; * for every element) and their category, sealed in run history when a run starts.

account_key.description: delivery app: the provider account an event is for (=body.team_id; =item.realmId with split).

revokes.description: delivery app: true for an event saying the business took Taskiem's app away (Slack's app_uninstalled): the account's connections are marked expired, and the event is delivered.

registration.description: manual (default): the provider is pointed at Taskiem's ingest URL by hand. remote: Taskiem creates, updates and deletes the provider's subscription as workflows using the trigger are deployed and removed, and verifies deliveries with the secret the provider returned (decision 0021); the connector supplies a registrar.

options.description: JSON Schema of the workflow trigger's options (trigger.config.options in wd/v1): what to subscribe to at the provider, and how to complete events.

test_event.description: Marks a delivery the provider sends to test the endpoint: it is verified and acknowledged, and starts only workflows that list its event by name.

title.description: A short name for what the trigger hears, in plain words (Payments, Transfers), shown next to its address on the Connections page.

where.description: Where the business pastes the trigger's address in the provider's dashboard, in one line, e.g. Paystack dashboard → Settings → API Keys & Webhooks → Live Webhook URL.

poll.description: Taskiem also asks the provider itself, for businesses that have not set the webhook up: a read action listing records since a time, each delivered as {event, data} signed with the connection's secret, so it takes the webhook's own checks and is taken once either way.

route.description: Routes a delivery a partner receives into its sub-tenants whose connection lists the event's key in field (decision 0031): key is an expression naming the account the event is about; field a non-secret auth field holding a comma-separated list.
